title: Bilinear metering experiment: asymmetric input/output minimums with stream smoothing
creator: Marina Gomez
description: Run a controlled field experiment that evaluates an asymmetric per-token billing model that applies separate anchored minimums for input and output tokens, with a bilinear smoothing function applied to streaming bursts to reduce cliff effects. Purpose is to understand behavioral and revenue impacts compared to the current symmetric minimum model.
background: Customers have reported economic surprise when short high-output streaming sessions trigger the global per-minute floor; existing experiments explored directional floors but left smoothing and asymmetric anchors untested. Our billing engine can already tag ingress vs egress tokens and apply per-direction floors; we need to validate real usage elasticity, churn risk, and operational complexity before recommending productization.
hypothesis: 1) Applying lower anchored minimums on input tokens and slightly higher anchors on output tokens will better reflect compute cost and reduce churn for chat-heavy customers. 2) Introducing a bilinear smoothing curve for short streaming bursts will reduce customer complaints from cliff billing while preserving revenue for heavy generators.
experiment_design:
- Sample: 8,000 eligible hosted API customers, randomized into 4 cohorts (control + 3 variants).
- Variant A: asymmetric anchors (input floor 0.6x baseline, output floor 1.2x baseline).
- Variant B: same asymmetric anchors + bilinear stream smoothing (0-5s heavy smoothing, 5-20s linear interpolation, >20s full floor).
- Variant C: symmetric anchors but with bilinear smoothing.
- Duration: 6 weeks, with 1-week ramp and 5-week steady analysis window.
- Implementation notes: experiment tags on billing pipeline, guardrails to backfill and reconcile discrepancies, and opt-out for accounts under active enterprise contracts.
metrics: Primary: net revenue per MAU, churn rate (% customers closing accounts or reducing spend), median cost per API call. Secondary: support ticket volume related to billing (label: billing-surprise), NPS delta for affected customers, estimated delta in unit economics (per-token margin). Also measure tail latency and quota enforcement incidents as safety checks.
gating_criteria: Proceed to wider rollout if: 1) revenue per MAU delta >= +3% vs control without increasing churn > 0.5 percentage points, OR 2) churn improves by >= 0.8 percentage points with no revenue degradation > 2%. If support volume doubles or we observe quota enforcement regressions, pause experiment and investigate.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal beta with 50 engineering/dev accounts for 7 days to validate billing tagging and smoothing logic. Phase 2: Ship experiment to randomized cohorts (8k sample) behind feature flag. Phase 3: Decision gate at 6 weeks to either iterate, scale to 25% of eligible population, or rollback to control. Final productization requires QA on invoices, documentation updates, and legal review for contract language.
risks_and_mitigation: Risks: 1) Invoicing divergence due to reconciliation bugs — mitigation: pre-run nightly reconciliation and debt safelist for any non-zero deltas. 2) Customer confusion — mitigation: include explanatory UI tooltip and link to pricing FAQ for experiment cohorts. 3) Enterprise contract conflicts — mitigation: exclude accounts with active negotiated terms; cross-check enterprise list before rollout.
notes: Coordinate with growth to ensure sampling excludes high-ARPU customers flagged by sales. Finance will need a dedicated report and a reconciliation playbook. Design to craft a short in-console explainer. Legal to review finished pricing language if rolling beyond pilot.
